about.title: Carlsbad Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Getting hurt at work in Carlsbad can leave you juggling medical visits, missed paychecks, and a stack of forms you never asked for. Most employees are covered by California workers' compensation, which pays for treatment and part of your lost wages no matter who was at fault. That system is usually your only claim against your employer itself. It is not always the end of the story, though. When someone outside your company contributed to the injury, whether a subcontractor on a job site, the owner of the building where you were working, the maker of a machine that failed, or another driver, a separate personal injury claim may be available alongside workers' comp. Driving is part of many Carlsbad jobs, and public records show 499 injury collisions in the city in 2025, with I-5, Palomar Airport Road, Carlsbad Boulevard, and El Camino Real carrying the highest counts. If a work-related crash or site accident hurt you, LawProactive can connect you at no cost with an independent attorney who can sort out which claims apply.

items.question: I was hit on Palomar Airport Road while driving for my job. Is workers' comp my only option?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Because you were working, workers' comp should cover your medical care and part of your wages regardless of fault. If another driver caused the crash, that driver is a third party, and you may also have a separate personal injury claim against them. An attorney can evaluate both together so neither one is overlooked.

items.question: Can my Carlsbad employer fire me for reporting an injury?
items.answer: No. Retaliating against an employee for reporting a workplace injury or filing a workers' comp claim is illegal in California. You should still report the injury to your employer within 30 days so the claim is properly on record. If you do face pushback, mention it to the attorney you speak with.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a claim after a work injury in San Diego County?
items.answer: There are two separate clocks. Report the injury to your employer within 30 days to protect your workers' comp benefits. A third-party personal injury claim, such as one against an equipment manufacturer or a property owner, generally must be filed within two years of the injury. Getting advice early gives you room to gather records and make decisions calmly.
